out:
{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the intervention training (based on the 4C/ID model and focused on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention) would improve performance in shoot/don't shoot scenarios compared to a traditional firearms training control group, specifically regarding response times and the time until the first hit.",
  "design": "mixed, 2 (group: intervention vs. control) x 2 (measurement time: pre-test vs. post-test)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "An individual video-based intervention training program grounded in the Four-Component Instructional Design Model (4C/ID), focusing on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention, compared to an active control group receiving traditional police firearms training.",
  "outcome_measure": "Time until the first hit (in milliseconds) in correctly detected shoot scenarios, measured during realistic shoot/don't shoot video scenarios.",
  "population_and_setting": "45 senior police officers recruited from the German Police University, tested in an indoor firing range lab setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 45,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via notices on campus; participation was voluntary.",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures ANOVA with the within-subject factor Time and the between-subject factor Group.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "preregistered",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants used a gas-operated replica of a Heckler and Koch SFP9 handgun. Eye-tracking was used during the pre- and post-test. The intervention training included an 18-minute educational video and practical exercises, while the control training included a 12-minute educational video and traditional marksmanship exercises."
}
